headline: Every major sits above its 200-day line while overbought readings stack up and whales keep walking coins onto exchanges
paragraphs: Start with regime, because the picture is unusually one-sided today. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB all sit above their 200-day moving averages, DOGE and ADA do not, and none of the seven has a golden cross yet. That's five of seven majors in a confirmed uptrend by this measure, which is a different market than the mixed, choppy tape this desk sometimes has to describe. BTC is up 21.8% on the month and 12.4% on the week, though flat on the day at up 0.04%. XRP is the month's standout among the majors at up 27.9%, with a week reading of up 26.0% behind it.

Momentum is where the first tension shows up. RSI-14 on BTC sits at 70.8, ETH at 70.2, and SOL at 75.1, all in territory a technician calls overbought, and MACD confirms the trend is still running (above signal) on every asset except ADA. That's not a divergence yet, momentum and trend agree, but stretched RSI on top of a trend that's already up over 20% on the month for BTC, ETH, and SOL is the kind of reading that tends to precede a rest, a pullback, or a sideways chop. It's a condition to note, not a signal to act on. ADA is the odd one out structurally: RSI at 52.4, MACD below signal, and price below the 200-day, all while still up 20.4% on the month. That's a laggard bouncing inside a still-broken trend.

Positioning tells a story of leverage without obvious excess. BTC funding on OKX sits at 0.0047% per 8 hours (5.1% annualized), which is mild, not the kind of expensive, crowded-long funding that usually precedes a flush. ETH funding is a bit hotter at 9.8% annualized. SOL funding is actually negative, -4.7% annualized, meaning shorts are paying longs there, an unusual setup given SOL's RSI of 75.1 and 40% monthly gain. Long/short account ratios lean long across the board (BTC 1.28, ETH 1.48, SOL 1.67, XRP 2.51, DOGE 3.94), and liquidations over the past 24 hours skew hard toward longs getting flushed: BTC longs lost $17.8M versus $2.1M in shorts, ETH longs lost $16.9M versus $3.0M in shorts. Open interest is largest in BTC ($2.24B) and ETH ($1.53B), meaning plenty of capital is riding this trend, and the long-side liquidations show some of it is getting tested in real time.

Flows are where the disagreement sharpens. The BTC spot ETF board posted an outflow of $201.9M on 28 Aug 2026, but the five-session net is a $924.5M inflow, only one day pointed in the outflow direction. Read the daily print for what it is, a single day, not a reversal. ETH ETFs are cleaner: an inflow of $102.1M on the same day, ten consecutive days in the same direction, and $815.7M net over five sessions, a flow picture with actual follow-through behind it. Meanwhile whale activity on BTC shows $98.4M moving onto exchanges over the last 24 hours (inflows of $756.7M against outflows of $658.3M), and the weekly pattern backs it up: three straight weeks ending Aug 15, Aug 22, and Aug 29 all show net flow onto exchanges, with the most recent week at $684M onto exchanges. Coins moving toward exchanges while ETF desks are still buying on a five-day basis is worth sitting with: it can mean profit-taking supply meeting institutional demand, or it can mean the reverse dynamics are about to test each other. The stablecoin float is up only 1.11% over 30 days to $309.8B, modest dry-powder growth, not a flood of fresh buying capacity.

Sentiment sits at 68, labeled Greed, near the top of its 30-day range of 25 to 74. That lines up with the price action (majors up double digits on the month) but sits awkwardly next to RSI readings already in overbought territory and whale wallets sending coins toward exchanges three weeks running. Total market cap fell 4.43% in the last 24 hours even as most majors show flat-to-slightly-positive daily moves, a mismatch worth noting rather than explaining away. What to watch from here: whether BTC funding stays cheap (currently 5.1% annualized) or climbs alongside price, whether the whale exchange-flow direction flips back to off-exchanges after three straight weekly prints onto exchanges, and whether the BTC ETF board's next few daily prints confirm or contradict the $924.5M five-session inflow now sitting against a single outflow day.
